claim_ceiling: External sources are boundary references and modeling inputs only; they are not upgraded into proved Ignition assets.

sources.exact_claim: Causal inference needs assumptions and a language that distinguishes observational distributions from intervention and counterfactual queries.
sources.assumptions: Structural causal models and graph/structural assumptions are required for identifying causal effects from data.
sources.usable_projection: Separate P(Y|X) from P(Y|do(X)); require identifiability and claim ceilings.
sources.forbidden_upgrade: Do not treat conditional probability or model fit as causal proof.
sources.citation: Judea Pearl, Causal Inference in Statistics: An Overview, Statistics Surveys 3 (2009), DOI 10.1214/09-SS057; https://projecteuclid.org/journals/statistics-surveys/volume-3/issue-none/Causal-inference-in-statistics-An-overview/10.1214/09-SS057.short

sources.exact_claim: Marked point-process graphs can encode local independences where event intensities are independent of parts of the past.
sources.assumptions: Continuous-time marked point-process setting with intensity-based dynamic dependence.
sources.usable_projection: Represent EventIntensityOrHazard with risk set, time window, and conditioning history.
sources.forbidden_upgrade: Do not treat any dynamic graph edge as identified causality without additional assumptions.
sources.citation: Vanessa Didelez, Graphical models for marked point processes based on local independence, arXiv:0710.5874; https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.5874

sources.exact_claim: Continuous-time counterfactual distributions can be characterized using stochastic analysis, martingale problems, local independence graphs, and likelihood-ratio reweighting under conditions.
sources.assumptions: Uniform integrability and model conditions are needed; graphical information does not remove assumptions.
sources.usable_projection: Represent InterventionDistribution separately from factual distribution and record identifiability conditions.
sources.forbidden_upgrade: Do not assume a counterfactual distribution exists or is identifiable without stated conditions.
sources.citation: Kjetil Røysland, Counterfactual analyses with graphical models based on local independence, arXiv:1106.0972; https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.0972

sources.exact_claim: Open systems exchange matter, energy, or information with their environment and cannot be treated as closed by default.
sources.assumptions: System boundary and environment are modeling choices and must be declared.
sources.usable_projection: Require SystemContext with boundary rule, environment, exchanges, and open/closed/hybrid status.
sources.forbidden_upgrade: Do not claim system boundaries are naturally unique or that every system is closed.
sources.citation: L. von Bertalanffy, The Theory of Open Systems in Physics and Biology, Science 111(2872):23-29, DOI 10.1126/science.111.2872.23; https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.111.2872.23

sources.exact_claim: Under a particular effective-information measure, macro causal models can supersede micro models for some systems.
sources.assumptions: Depends on chosen micro/macro map, state space, intervention distribution, and EI measure.
sources.usable_projection: Represent CoarseGrainingEmergenceRecord with map, information loss, comparator, and claim ceiling.
sources.forbidden_upgrade: Do not claim macro levels always beat micro levels or that correlation after coarse-graining proves emergence.
sources.citation: Erik P. Hoel, Larissa Albantakis, Giulio Tononi, Quantifying causal emergence shows that macro can beat micro, PNAS, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1314922110; https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.1314922110

sources.exact_claim: Nonequilibrium thermodynamics on causal networks can include informational quantities in generalized second-law and fluctuation-theorem settings.
sources.assumptions: Stochastic thermodynamic systems and causal-network modeling assumptions are required.
sources.usable_projection: Separate information entropy/flow fields from thermodynamic entropy production and record assumptions.
sources.forbidden_upgrade: Do not equate Shannon information entropy with thermodynamic entropy without system-specific assumptions.
sources.citation: Sosuke Ito and Takahiro Sagawa, Information Thermodynamics on Causal Networks, arXiv:1306.2756 / Phys. Rev. Lett. 111, 180603; https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.2756

sources.exact_claim: The filtering and prediction problem can be formulated using state-transition methods for linear dynamic systems.
sources.assumptions: Linear filtering and prediction framework; later common Kalman filtering uses linear-Gaussian assumptions in many forms.
sources.usable_projection: Represent StateSpace, ObservabilityControllabilityRecord, and estimator boundary conditions.
sources.forbidden_upgrade: Do not treat linear, Gaussian, or fully observable assumptions as universal system laws.
sources.citation: R. E. Kalman, A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction Problems, Journal of Basic Engineering 82(1):35-45, DOI 10.1115/1.3662552; https://asmedigitalcollection.asme.org/fluidsengineering/article/82/1/35/397706/A-New-Approach-to-Linear-Filtering-and-Prediction
